stops.name: The Counter
stops.intro: Start or resume a session from Study.
steps: Choose Practice, Flashcards, or Exam. Resume appears when a session is available.
Choose a subject and 5, 10, or 20 questions. Customize opens pools, difficulty, and topics.
Your setup is remembered after a successful start. Bookmarked questions, notes, saved sets, and progress remain nearby.

screens.alt: Study groups session modes, Resume, and quick setup on one screen. This image uses synthetic software test questions.
screens.caption: Study groups session modes, Resume, and quick setup on one screen. This image uses synthetic software test questions.

stops.name: Fresh Catch
stops.intro: Choose the subjects and mix for your daily ten.
steps: Edit subjects and optionally customize the unseen/missed mix.
Answer each question. Check answer opens feedback during the catch.
At question ten, choose Finish catch. Review unanswered items first when prompted.
Your completion screen confirms the score and daily stamp.

screens.alt: The last question provides an explicit Finish catch action after all answers are saved.
screens.caption: The last question provides an explicit Finish catch action after all answers are saved.

stops.name: Memory Maki
stops.intro: Answer, learn from the feedback, then rate your familiarity.
steps: Start quickly from the Flashcards tab on Study, or use the advanced deck setup to choose exact cards.
Answer, then read the explanation, alternatives, and source inline. Bookmark, Make a note, and Report a problem have separate controls.
Rate recall with 1 Again, 2 Hard, 3 Okay, 4 Good, or 5 Easy. How recall ratings work explains the weighting beside the buttons.
Use the menu for deck progress or Finish session. At 80% rated 5, you can finish or keep going.

screens.alt: A focused question with progress and secondary tools in the menu.
screens.caption: A focused question with progress and secondary tools in the menu.

screens.alt: Inline feedback and separate question tools sit above the recall grades. This image uses a synthetic software test question.
screens.caption: Inline feedback and separate question tools sit above the recall grades. This image uses a synthetic software test question.

stops.name: Mentor and Rush
stops.intro: Choose practice or a timed exam.
steps: Use the Practice tab on Study for feedback after each checked answer.
Use the Exam tab for a timed session with feedback after submission.
Customize links to advanced setup for balanced subjects, exact questions, and exam quotas.

screens.alt: A topic review starts a focused practice session. This image uses a synthetic test account.
screens.caption: A topic review starts a focused practice session. This image uses a synthetic test account.

screens.alt: The Exam tab adds a time limit to shared setup. This image uses a synthetic test account.
screens.caption: The Exam tab adds a time limit to shared setup. This image uses a synthetic test account.

stops.name: Roll Call
stops.intro: Browse the bank and choose exactly what to study.
steps: Search by text or question ID and narrow the subject.
Switch among all, unseen, missed, and saved questions.
Add questions to the study tray, then start a practice round or Memory Maki deck.
Use private notes for your reasoning or report a question for Head Chef to review.

screens.alt: Roll Call combines search, saved questions, and a study tray.
screens.caption: Roll Call combines search, saved questions, and a study tray.

stops.name: Bento Builder
stops.intro: Create a reviewed exam and downloadable PDF set.
steps: Choose coverage or load a saved class recipe.
Allocate questions evenly, by subject count, or by topic and difficulty quotas.
Preview the actual questions and replace any item before saving.
Save the bento, then prepare the exam paper, answer sheet, and answer key PDFs.

screens.alt: Build an exam from selected subjects, topics, and reviewable question counts.
screens.caption: Build an exam from selected subjects, topics, and reviewable question counts.

stops.name: Progress and crew
stops.intro: See your learning patterns and collect your sushi crew.
steps: Open Filters, choose your criteria, then Apply filters.
First-answer accuracy, questions covered, and questions needing review use the same filters. Need review uses the latest overall released answer.
Choose Review next or review a topic to start up to 20 matching questions.
Older lifetime summaries remain labeled below the filtered cards. Passport and your profile keep achievements available.

screens.alt: Filtered progress cards include direct review actions. This image uses a synthetic test account.
screens.caption: Filtered progress cards include direct review actions. This image uses a synthetic test account.

screens.alt: Achievement cards show their character, requirement, and earned status.
screens.caption: Achievement cards show their character, requirement, and earned status.

stops.name: Head Chef
stops.intro: Manage learners, class practice, and the question bank.
steps: Open Head Chef from your account menu whenever you need the administrator tools.
Add learners individually or preview a CSV roster to create invitation links.
Use the quality queue to review questions and preserve corrections as new versions.
Share class recipes, assign saved exams, and inspect cohort progress or backup status.
